sections.name: General Knowledge
sections.note: Part 1 (VALR, DM, QADI) shares a combined 170-minute limit; GK is a separate 10-minute section with no negative marking.

items.passage: For most of human history, scarcity lived in things: food, shelter, tools. Today, in wealthy economies, scarcity has moved into attention. Information is abundant and cheap, but the hours in which a person can attend to it are fixed. Firms therefore compete less on what they can produce than on what they can make noticeable. This shift changes how value is created. A product that is merely good may fail if it never enters awareness, while a mediocre product with a compelling story can dominate a market for years. Critics argue that this rewards manipulation over merit, and that platforms profit by keeping users unsettled rather than satisfied. Defenders reply that attention has always shaped markets, from shop signs to newspaper headlines, and that the new tools only make an old contest more visible. Both sides miss a subtler point. Attention is not only a resource to be captured; it is also the medium through which people decide what matters. When the loudest voice wins, public judgement narrows. When quieter, careful work gets time to be understood, judgement deepens. The question is therefore not whether attention markets exist, but what kind of attention a society chooses to reward.
items.question: According to the passage, what has become scarce in wealthy economies?
items.explanation: The passage states that information is abundant but the hours in which a person can attend to it are fixed, so attention is the scarce resource. Physical goods are described as historically scarce, not currently scarce. Capital and labour are not identified as the new scarcity.

items.question: The author suggests that a mediocre product can dominate a market because
options: it enters public awareness through a compelling story
it is cheaper to produce than good products
items.explanation: The passage says a mediocre product with a compelling story can dominate for years while a merely good product may fail if it never enters awareness. Price, regulation and consumer inability are not given as the reasons. The mechanism is visibility through story.

items.question: Which of the following best captures the author's subtler point?
options: Attention shapes what a society judges to matter
Attention markets are entirely new and unprecedented
Manipulation always defeats merit in the long run
Platforms should be banned from competing for attention
items.explanation: The author says attention is the medium through which people decide what matters, and the question is what kind of attention society rewards. The passage explicitly notes attention contests are old, not entirely new. It does not claim manipulation always wins or call for a ban.

items.question: The tone of the passage is best described as
items.explanation: The author weighs critics and defenders, finds both miss a point, and ends with a reflective question, which is analytical and balanced. There is no outrage, sarcasm or celebration in the wording.

items.passage: Every large organisation faces the same tension: rules bring consistency, while discretion brings judgement. Rules protect against favouritism and error, and they let newcomers act correctly without years of experience. Yet rules written for yesterday's cases often misfire on today's exceptions. A loan officer who follows the checklist exactly may reject a sound borrower whose papers look unusual; a doctor bound by a rigid protocol may miss what the patient in front of them plainly needs. The usual remedy is to add more rules, to cover the exceptions, but each new rule creates fresh edge cases of its own. The alternative is to invest in judgement: hire carefully, train deeply, review decisions openly, and accept that some mistakes will happen. Organisations that choose this path are slower to scale and harder to audit, but their decisions age better when circumstances change. The wisest firms do not pick one side permanently. They write rules for the routine, reserve discretion for the unusual, and keep a record of when discretion was used and why, so that today's judgement can become tomorrow's better rule.
items.question: The central tension described in the passage is between
items.explanation: The opening sentence frames the tension as rules bringing consistency while discretion brings judgement. The other pairs are not the framing used in the passage.

items.question: Why does adding more rules often fail, according to the author?
options: Each new rule creates fresh edge cases
Rules are too expensive to enforce
Employees refuse to follow new rules
items.explanation: The passage states each new rule creates fresh edge cases of its own, so rule proliferation cannot close the gap. Refusal, cost and customer dislike are not cited.

items.question: The author recommends that discretion should be
options: used for unusual cases and recorded with reasons
items.explanation: The passage recommends writing rules for the routine, reserving discretion for the unusual, and keeping a record of when it was used and why. Elimination and unreviewed use contradict the argument, and senior-only restriction is not stated.

items.question: Which assumption underlies the author's preference for investing in judgement?
options: Circumstances change, so rigid rules age poorly
Mistakes can be eliminated entirely by training
Audits are unnecessary in well-run firms
items.explanation: The author says decisions based on judgement age better when circumstances change, which assumes change makes rigid rules stale. Training is said to reduce but not eliminate mistakes, since some mistakes will happen. Audits and newcomer learning are not the basis of the claim.

items.question: Choose the word closest in meaning to PRUDENT.
items.explanation: Prudent means acting with care and thought for the future, so cautious is the closest synonym. Reckless and hasty are near opposites, and lavish concerns extravagant spending rather than careful judgement.

items.question: Choose the word closest in meaning to CANDID.
items.explanation: Candid means truthful and straightforward, so frank is the closest synonym. Secretive and vague are opposites in sense, and polite describes manner rather than honesty.

items.question: Choose the word opposite in meaning to TRANSPARENT.
items.explanation: Transparent means allowing light through or easy to understand, so opaque is the direct opposite. Clear and obvious are synonyms, and honest is a related but different quality.

items.question: Choose the word opposite in meaning to ABUNDANT.
items.explanation: Abundant means existing in large quantities, so scarce is the opposite. Plentiful, ample and copious are all synonyms of abundant.

items.question: Choose the word closest in meaning to EPHEMERAL.
items.explanation: Ephemeral means lasting for a very short time, so short-lived is the synonym. Eternal and ancient imply long duration, and sturdy concerns strength rather than duration.

items.question: Choose the word closest in meaning to PRAGMATIC.
items.explanation: Pragmatic means dealing with problems in a practical rather than theoretical way, so practical is closest. Idealistic and theoretical point the other way, and dogmatic means rigidly holding opinions.

items.question: Choose the word opposite in meaning to BENEVOLENT.
items.explanation: Benevolent means well-meaning and kindly, so malevolent, meaning having ill will, is the opposite. Kind, generous and charitable are all synonyms.

items.question: Choose the word closest in meaning to METICULOUS.
items.explanation: Meticulous means showing great attention to detail, so thorough is the closest synonym. Careless, hasty and casual all suggest the opposite lack of care.

items.question: Choose the word closest in meaning to AMBIGUOUS.
items.explanation: Ambiguous means open to more than one interpretation, so uncertain captures that sense best. Clear, definite and obvious all imply a single settled meaning.

items.question: Choose the word opposite in meaning to DILIGENT.
items.explanation: Diligent means showing steady careful effort, so lazy is the opposite. Industrious, careful and persistent are synonyms or near synonyms.

items.question: Fill in the blank: The committee reached a decision only after a ______ debate that lasted six hours.
items.explanation: A debate lasting six hours is long and drawn out, so protracted fits. Cursory means brief, trivial means unimportant, and silent contradicts a debate taking place.

items.question: Fill in the blank: Despite the setback, the team remained ______ and continued working towards the deadline.
items.explanation: Continuing to work towards the deadline despite a setback shows determination, so resolute fits. Despondent means disheartened, indifferent means uncaring, and hostile means unfriendly.

items.question: Fill in the blank: The report was criticised for its ______ claims, which were not supported by any data.
items.explanation: Claims not supported by data are unfounded. Substantiated and verified mean supported by evidence, and measured means careful, which does not fit unsupported claims.

items.question: Fill in the blank: Good leaders listen carefully before speaking, because a ______ remark can damage trust that took years to build.
items.explanation: A remark that damages trust built over years is one made too quickly, so hasty fits. Considered, thoughtful and guarded all describe careful speech, which would protect rather than damage trust.

items.question: Identify the grammatically correct sentence.
options: Neither of the answers is correct.
Neither of the answers are correct.
Neither of the answer are correct.
Neither of the answers were correct.
items.explanation: Neither takes a singular verb, and the plural noun answers needs the singular is after neither of. The other options mismatch subject and verb or use a singular noun incorrectly.

items.question: Identify the grammatically correct sentence.
options: Each of the students are submitting the form.
Each of the students has submitted the form.
Each of the students have submitted the form.
Each of the student has submitted the form.
items.explanation: Each is singular and takes has, even though it is followed by the plural students. Have and are are plural verbs, and student should be plural after each of the.

items.question: Identify the grammatically correct sentence.
options: The team, along with the coach, are travelling tomorrow.
The team, along with the coach, is travelling tomorrow.
The team, along with the coach, were travelling tomorrow.
The team along with the coach are travelling tomorrow.
items.explanation: The subject is the team, singular, and along with the coach does not change its number, so is is correct. Are and were are plural and do not agree with the singular subject.

items.question: Identify the sentence with NO grammatical error.
options: She suggested he to apply early.
She suggested that he apply early.
She suggested him to apply early.
She suggested to him to apply early.
items.explanation: Suggest is followed by a that clause with the base verb, so that he apply is correct. Suggest does not take an object plus infinitive, so the other forms are ungrammatical.

items.passage: A mid-sized food company discovers that one batch of its packaged snacks may contain traces of a nut allergen not listed on the label. Only a small number of packs are affected, and no illness has been reported. Recalling the batch will cost a large sum and damage a new product launch. The quality head wants an immediate recall; the sales head argues for quiet withdrawal from stores without a public notice, saying a public recall would cause panic out of proportion to the risk.
items.question: What is the most responsible course of action for the company?
options: Issue a public recall with clear batch details and a refund process
Quietly withdraw packs from stores without telling customers
Offer discounts on the next batch to affected buyers
Wait for an illness report before acting
items.explanation: A public recall with batch details and refunds protects allergic customers who may already hold packs at home, which quiet withdrawal cannot do. Waiting for harm and offering discounts both leave the risk in place and breach the duty to warn.

items.question: The sales head's argument is weakest because it
options: assumes panic is worse than the health risk to allergic customers
ignores the cost of a recall
items.explanation: The argument weighs reputational panic against a health risk but treats panic as the greater harm, which reverses the priority owed to allergic customers. Cost and timetable are real concerns but are not the logical weakness in the panic argument.

items.question: If the company chooses a public recall, what should it do first?
options: Announce a new product to distract attention
Ask retailers to handle all complaints alone
Publish the affected batch numbers and helpline before any other message
Blame the supplier in the press release
items.explanation: Affected customers need batch numbers and a helpline immediately to check packs they hold. Blaming a supplier, distracting with a launch, or leaving retailers alone all delay the safety information that matters most.

items.passage: A sales team has one outstanding performer who regularly exceeds targets but routinely ignores reporting rules, misses team meetings, and takes credit for colleagues' work. Junior members are demoralised, and two have asked for transfers. The manager must decide whether to discipline the performer, risking a sharp fall in team revenue, or tolerate the behaviour to keep numbers strong.
items.question: What should the manager prioritise?
options: Ignoring the complaints until the quarter ends
Transferring the junior members who complained
Fair process and team health, with clear consequences for the performer
items.explanation: Tolerating credit-taking and rule-breaking trades lasting team health for one quarter's numbers and signals that results excuse conduct. Fair process with clear consequences protects the team while giving the performer a chance to change.

items.question: Which action best balances revenue and fairness?
options: Promise the juniors a bonus if they stay quiet
Publicly shame the performer in a team meeting
Give the performer a private warning with specific behaviours, a deadline, and measurable team conduct goals
Cut the performer's targets so the behaviour matters less
items.explanation: A private warning with specific behaviours, a deadline and measurable goals is proportionate and preserves dignity while making change verifiable. Public shaming, cutting targets and buying silence all avoid the real issue or create new unfairness.

items.question: If the performer improves reporting but still takes credit for others' work, the manager should
options: Address the remaining credit-taking directly, since it drives the demoralisation
Move the performer to a solo role without discussion
Increase the performer's bonus to encourage more change
items.explanation: Credit-taking is the behaviour driving demoralisation, so it must be addressed directly rather than treated as settled by partial improvement. A silent transfer or a bonus avoids the conversation the team needs to see happen.

items.passage: A procurement officer is offered an expensive gift by a supplier bidding for a large contract. The supplier's product is genuinely good and competitively priced. The officer's firm has a strict no-gift policy, but the officer believes refusing will offend the supplier and that accepting will not affect the decision, since the supplier would win on merit anyway.
items.question: What should the procurement officer do?
options: Decline the gift and disclose the offer to the compliance team
Accept the gift but declare it after the contract is awarded
Accept the gift, since the supplier would win on merit
Ask a colleague to accept it instead
items.explanation: Declining and disclosing protects both the officer and the fairness of the process, since even a merit-based win looks tainted after a gift. Accepting, deferring disclosure, or routing through a colleague all create the appearance and risk of influence.

items.question: The officer's belief that acceptance will not affect the decision is flawed because
options: the compliance team is always suspicious
gifts create obligation and the appearance of bias even when intentions are good
gifts are illegal in every country
items.explanation: Gifts create a sense of obligation and make a later merit-based decision look biased, which is why no-gift policies exist. Product quality does not remove that effect, and the point is about appearance and obligation, not universal illegality.

items.question: Which safeguard best protects future tenders?
options: Awarding contracts only to the lowest bidder
Letting officers decide gifts case by case
A clear no-gift rule, disclosed evaluation criteria, and independent review of awards
items.explanation: A clear rule plus disclosed criteria and independent review removes ambiguity and lets losers verify fairness. Case-by-case discretion, secret criteria and lowest-price-only rules each create new avenues for bias or poor quality.

items.passage: A small health-tech firm learns that a software flaw exposed some users' health records for two weeks. The flaw is now fixed, and the firm cannot tell whose records were actually viewed. The founders debate whether to notify all users, which will alarm many whose data was never accessed, or to notify only those they can prove were affected, which may be almost no one.
items.question: What is the most defensible notification approach?
options: Say nothing, since the flaw is fixed
Wait for a regulator to order notification
Notify all potentially affected users honestly about what is known and unknown
items.explanation: Notifying all potentially affected users with an honest account of what is known and unknown respects their right to protect themselves. Silence, complaint-only notice and waiting for an order all leave users unable to act on a risk the firm created.

items.question: The founders' concern about alarming unaffected users is best addressed by
options: Exaggerating the risk so users take it seriously
Clear, factual communication explaining the exposure window, the fix, and the steps users can take
items.explanation: Clear factual communication lets users judge their own risk without panic or false reassurance. Hiding, exaggerating and blaming all distort the information users need to decide.

items.question: Beyond notification, what should the firm prioritise?
options: A marketing campaign to restore its image
Reducing the features that store health data
Suing the users who raise concerns
An independent security audit, a fix review, and a written incident process
items.explanation: An independent audit, a review of the fix and a written incident process address the root cause and prevent recurrence. Marketing, suing users and cutting features without diagnosis treat symptoms or punish the harmed party.

items.passage: A factory must cut costs by 15 percent. The management team can either lay off 60 junior workers, close one small plant and move its 40 workers to other sites with retraining, or cut pay by 10 percent for all 400 staff. Each option harms someone, and the union opposes all three.
items.question: Which factor should weigh most heavily in choosing between the options?
options: The long-term effect on livelihoods, skills, and the firm's ability to recover
Which option is easiest to announce
Which option the union dislikes least in the first meeting
Which option protects senior managers' pay
items.explanation: Long-term effects on livelihoods, retained skills and recovery capacity determine whether the cut saves the firm or hollows it out. Ease of announcement, first-meeting reaction and protecting senior pay are poor guides to a decision with lasting consequences.

items.question: The pay-cut option's main risk is that it
options: requires union approval in every country
may drive away the most employable staff, who can leave most easily
items.explanation: Across-the-board pay cuts often push out the most employable staff first, leaving the firm weaker. The option is not universally illegal or necessarily costlier, and approval rules vary, so those are not its main risk.

items.question: What process would make any chosen option most acceptable?
options: Choosing the option with the least press coverage
Transparent sharing of the financial position, genuine consultation, and support for those affected
items.explanation: Transparent finances, genuine consultation and support for affected staff give the decision legitimacy even when the outcome hurts. Silent announcement, press avoidance and fragmented decisions all undermine trust.

items.passage: A startup founder is preparing a pitch to investors. The finance lead has prepared a realistic forecast showing modest growth. The founder wants to present a far more optimistic forecast, arguing that investors expect ambition and that the team will work harder to meet a stretch target. The finance lead worries the optimistic numbers will mislead investors and set the team up to fail.
items.question: What should the founder present to investors?
options: The optimistic forecast, with the realistic one hidden
The realistic forecast with clearly labelled stretch scenarios and the assumptions behind each
Only the optimistic forecast, since ambition attracts funding
items.explanation: A realistic base case plus labelled stretch scenarios with assumptions lets investors judge ambition honestly. Presenting only optimism misleads, hiding the realistic case is deception, and no forecast leaves investors unable to assess the plan.

items.question: The founder's stretch-target argument fails because
options: it confuses an internal motivational tool with an external disclosure to investors
items.explanation: A stretch target can motivate a team internally, but presenting it to investors as the expected case misrepresents the outlook. The flaw is the category error between motivation and disclosure, not that ambition or stretch goals are worthless.

items.question: If investors fund the startup on the optimistic forecast and growth falls short, the most likely consequence is
options: Loss of investor trust and pressure to cut corners to meet the promised numbers
The team will be praised for ambition
items.explanation: Missing promised numbers after an optimistic pitch damages trust and creates pressure to hit the numbers by cutting corners. Praise, automatic funding and no consequence all ignore how investor trust works.

items.passage: A junior consultant discovers that a senior colleague's winning client proposal reused large sections from a competitor's public case study without attribution. The client is delighted with the proposal. Reporting it could cost the firm the contract and damage the senior colleague's career. Staying silent keeps the contract but leaves the firm exposed if the copying is discovered.
items.question: What should the junior consultant do?
options: Tell the client anonymously at once
Raise the concern privately with the senior colleague and then with a manager or ethics channel if unresolved
Copy the same approach in future proposals
Stay silent to protect the contract
items.explanation: Raising the concern privately first, then escalating through a proper channel if unresolved, gives the firm a chance to fix the issue while protecting the consultant. Silence leaves the exposure in place, anonymous disclosure skips internal remedy, and copying repeats the misconduct.

items.question: The strongest reason to act is that
options: the copying creates legal and reputational risk for the firm and misleads the client
the client is too easily pleased
the senior colleague dislikes the junior
items.explanation: Unattributed reuse misleads the client and exposes the firm to legal and reputational risk, which is a firm-level reason to act. Personal dislike, client gullibility and industry practice do not justify or outweigh that risk.

items.question: What should the firm do about the proposal itself?
options: Destroy all copies and deny it existed
Keep the proposal and hope nobody notices
Withdraw or correct the proposal and disclose the issue to the client as appropriate
items.explanation: Withdrawing or correcting the proposal and disclosing as appropriate removes the misleading material and restores honesty with the client. Hoping, blaming and denying all preserve the deception and increase the eventual damage.

items.question: The average of 5 numbers is 27. If one number is removed, the average of the remaining numbers becomes 25. What is the number that was removed?
items.explanation: The sum of the five numbers is 5 x 27 = 135. The sum of the remaining four is 4 x 25 = 100. The removed number is therefore 135 - 100 = 35. The other options come from miscomputing one of the two sums.

items.question: A can finish a job in 12 days and B can finish the same job in 18 days. Working together, in how many days will they finish the job?
items.explanation: A does 1/12 of the job per day and B does 1/18, so together they do 1/12 + 1/18 = 5/36 of the job per day. The time needed is 36/5 = 7.2 days. Simply averaging 12 and 18 gives 15 days, which is wrong because rates add, not times.

items.question: The sum of the present ages of A and B is 40 years. Five years ago, A was twice as old as B. What is the present age of A?
items.explanation: Let A be x years now, so B is 40 - x. Five years ago A was x - 5 and B was 35 - x, and x - 5 = 2(35 - x), which gives 3x = 75, so x = 25. Checking: five years ago A was 20 and B was 10, exactly twice as old.

items.question: A shopkeeper marks his goods 40% above cost price and then gives a discount of 20% on the marked price. What is his profit percentage?
items.explanation: Take cost price as 100. The marked price is 140, and after a 20% discount the selling price is 140 x 0.80 = 112. The profit is 12 on a cost of 100, so 12%. Adding 40% and subtracting 20% to get 20% is wrong because the discount applies to the marked price, not the cost.

items.question: What is the difference between the compound interest and the simple interest on Rs 10,000 for 2 years at 10% per annum?
items.explanation: The difference between compound and simple interest for two years equals P x (r/100)^2 = 10,000 x 0.01 = Rs 100. The compound interest is Rs 2,100 and the simple interest is Rs 2,000, and their difference is Rs 100.

items.question: A train 240 metres long crosses a pole in 12 seconds. What is the speed of the train in km/h?
items.explanation: Speed is 240/12 = 20 metres per second. Converting to km/h means multiplying by 18/5, so 20 x 18/5 = 72 km/h. Forgetting the conversion leaves 20, which is not among the options in the right unit, and using 5/18 instead gives a far smaller value.

items.question: A mixture contains milk and water in the ratio 5:3. If 16 litres of water is added, the ratio becomes 5:4. How much milk does the mixture contain?
items.explanation: Let milk be 5x and water be 3x litres. After adding water, 5x/(3x + 16) = 5/4, so 20x = 15x + 80, giving x = 16. Milk is 5 x 16 = 80 litres. The water added changes only the water part, so the milk quantity stays fixed at its original value.

items.question: If x^2 - 7x + 12 = 0, what is the sum of the squares of its roots?
items.explanation: The equation factors as (x - 3)(x - 4) = 0, so the roots are 3 and 4, and the sum of their squares is 9 + 16 = 25. Equivalently, (sum of roots)^2 - 2(product) = 49 - 24 = 25. The value 27 would come from adding the roots themselves to the product.

items.question: A right-angled triangle has legs of length 9 cm and 12 cm. What is the circumradius of the triangle?
items.explanation: The hypotenuse is sqrt(9^2 + 12^2) = sqrt(225) = 15 cm. In a right triangle the hypotenuse is a diameter of the circumcircle, so the circumradius is half the hypotenuse, 7.5 cm. The value 15 cm is the diameter, not the radius.

items.question: If log2(x) + log2(x - 2) = 3, what is the value of x?
items.explanation: Combining the logs gives log2(x(x - 2)) = 3, so x^2 - 2x = 8, or x^2 - 2x - 8 = 0. This factors as (x - 4)(x + 2) = 0. Since x must exceed 2 for the log to be defined, x = 4, and the negative root is rejected.

items.question: What is the sum of the first 20 terms of an arithmetic progression whose first term is 3 and common difference is 4?
items.explanation: The sum is n/2 x [2a + (n - 1)d] = 20/2 x [6 + 19 x 4] = 10 x 82 = 820. The 20th term is 3 + 19 x 4 = 79, and pairing terms from the ends (3 + 79, 7 + 75, and so on) also gives 10 pairs of 82.

items.question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 6 hours while pipe B can empty it in 8 hours. If both pipes are opened together, in how many hours will the tank be filled?
items.explanation: A fills 1/6 of the tank per hour and B empties 1/8, so the net fill rate is 1/6 - 1/8 = 1/24 per hour. The tank therefore takes 24 hours to fill. Adding the rates instead of subtracting them would wrongly give about 3.4 hours.

items.question: What is the volume of a cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 10 cm? (Use pi = 22/7)
items.explanation: Volume is pi x r^2 x h = (22/7) x 49 x 10 = 22 x 7 x 10 = 1540 cubic cm. Using 49 x 10 = 490 and multiplying by 22/7 gives 1540; the other options come from arithmetic slips in that multiplication.

items.question: A man sells an article at Rs 960 after giving a 20% discount on the marked price, and still makes a profit of 20%. What is the cost price of the article?
items.explanation: The marked price is 960/0.80 = Rs 1,200. Since the selling price of Rs 960 is 20% above cost, the cost price is 960/1.20 = Rs 800. Working backwards from the marked price without removing the profit gives the wrong value of Rs 1,000.

items.question: What is the remainder when 7^2025 is divided by 5?
items.explanation: Modulo 5, 7 is 2, and powers of 2 cycle 2, 4, 3, 1 with period 4. Since 2025 leaves remainder 1 on division by 4, 7^2025 is congruent to 2^1 = 2 modulo 5. The cycle must be tracked from the base 2, not from 7 itself.

items.question: Two fair dice are thrown. What is the probability that the sum of the numbers shown is 9?
items.explanation: There are 36 equally likely outcomes. The pairs summing to 9 are (3,6), (4,5), (5,4) and (6,3), which is 4 outcomes, so the probability is 4/36 = 1/9. Counting only (3,6) and (4,5) and forgetting order would give 2/36, which is wrong.

items.question: In how many ways can 5 people be seated in a row if two particular people must sit together?
items.explanation: Treat the two people as a single block, which can be arranged with the other three in 4! = 24 ways, and the two people inside the block can swap places in 2 ways. The total is 24 x 2 = 48. Forgetting the internal swap halves the answer to 24.

items.question: In triangle ABC, AB = 13 cm, BC = 14 cm and CA = 15 cm. What is the area of the triangle?
items.explanation: The semi-perimeter is (13 + 14 + 15)/2 = 21. By Heron's formula the area is sqrt(21 x 8 x 7 x 6) = sqrt(7056) = 84 sq cm. This is the classic 13-14-15 triangle, whose area is 84; the other options come from using the wrong semi-perimeter.

items.question: If x + 1/x = 5, what is the value of x^2 + 1/x^2?
items.explanation: Squaring both sides gives x^2 + 2 + 1/x^2 = 25, so x^2 + 1/x^2 = 23. The value 25 comes from forgetting to subtract the cross term 2 that appears on squaring.

items.question: Two trains, 200 m and 300 m long, run towards each other at 54 km/h and 36 km/h. How long do they take to completely cross each other?
items.explanation: The relative speed is 54 + 36 = 90 km/h, which is 25 m/s. The total distance to cover is 200 + 300 = 500 m, so the time is 500/25 = 20 seconds. Using only one train's speed, or one train's length, gives the wrong time.

items.question: A batsman has an average of 40 runs after 20 innings. After his 21st innings his average rises to 41. How many runs did he score in the 21st innings?
items.explanation: After 20 innings his total is 20 x 40 = 800 runs. After 21 innings his total is 21 x 41 = 861 runs. The 21st innings therefore contributed 861 - 800 = 61 runs. The rise of 1 in the average over 21 innings means the new innings scored 41 + 20 = 61.

items.question: How many integers between 1 and 100 (both inclusive) are divisible by 3 or by 5?
items.explanation: There are 33 multiples of 3, 20 multiples of 5, and 6 multiples of 15 in the range. By inclusion-exclusion the count is 33 + 20 - 6 = 47. Adding 33 and 20 without subtracting the overlap double-counts the multiples of 15.

items.question: Which firm had the highest total revenue over the four quarters?

diagram.caption: Quarterly revenue (Rs crore) of four firms, FY 2025-26

items.explanation: Adding the four quarters: A = 120 + 150 + 180 + 210 = 660, B = 200 + 180 + 220 + 240 = 840, C = 90 + 110 + 130 + 150 = 480, D = 160 + 140 + 170 + 190 = 660. Firm B has the highest total at Rs 840 crore, well ahead of A and D at 660 each.

items.question: What is the percentage growth in Firm A's revenue from Q1 to Q4?
items.explanation: Firm A's revenue rose from Rs 120 crore in Q1 to Rs 210 crore in Q4, an increase of 90 crore. The percentage growth is 90/120 x 100 = 75%. Using Q4 as the base instead of Q1 would wrongly give about 43%.

items.question: In which quarter was the combined revenue of all four firms the highest, and by how much did it exceed the lowest quarter?
items.explanation: The combined totals are Q1 = 570, Q2 = 580, Q3 = 700 and Q4 = 790 crore. The highest is Q4 at 790 and the lowest is Q1 at 570, so Q4 exceeds Q1 by 220 crore. Q3 is the second highest but trails Q4 by 90 crore.

items.question: What is the overall percentage increase in total employees from 2023 to 2024?

diagram.caption: Number of employees by department, 2023 and 2024

items.explanation: Total employees in 2023 were 240 + 60 + 180 + 90 + 300 = 870, and in 2024 they were 260 + 55 + 210 + 85 + 320 = 930. The increase is 60 on a base of 870, which is 60/870 x 100 = 6.9%. Averaging the departmental growth rates instead would give a different, wrong figure.

items.question: Which department recorded the highest percentage growth in headcount?
items.explanation: Growth rates are: Sales 20/240 = 8.33%, HR -8.33%, IT 30/180 = 16.67%, Finance -5.56%, Operations 20/300 = 6.67%. IT has the highest percentage growth at 16.67%, even though Operations added a similar absolute number on a much larger base.

items.question: What is the ratio of IT employees to HR employees in 2024?
items.explanation: In 2024 IT had 210 employees and HR had 55, so the ratio is 210:55. Dividing both sides by 5 gives 42:11. The ratio 21:11 would come from halving only the IT figure, which is not valid.

items.question: Which organisation publishes the World Economic Outlook report?
items.explanation: The World Economic Outlook is the International Monetary Fund's flagship publication on global economic prospects, released twice a year. The World Bank publishes the Global Economic Prospects, and the WTO focuses on trade, not this report.

items.question: Who is known as the Father of the Indian Constitution?
items.explanation: Dr B. R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly and is regarded as the chief architect of the Indian Constitution. Nehru moved the Objectives Resolution and Patel integrated the princely states, but the drafting leadership belonged to Ambedkar.

items.question: The headquarters of the United Nations is located in which city?
items.explanation: The United Nations headquarters is in New York City, United States. Geneva hosts many UN agencies such as the WHO and the WTO, but the main headquarters and the General Assembly meet in New York.

items.question: Which Indian state is the largest producer of coffee?
items.explanation: Karnataka produces more than two-thirds of India's coffee, mainly from the districts of Chikmagalur, Kodagu and Hassan. Kerala and Tamil Nadu also grow coffee but on a much smaller scale, and Assam is known for tea.

items.question: The headquarters of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) is located in which city?
items.explanation: SEBI is headquartered in Mumbai, the centre of India's capital markets, with regional offices in Delhi, Kolkata, Chennai and Ahmedabad. The RBI is also headquartered in Mumbai, while most ministries sit in New Delhi.

items.question: Who wrote the book 'The Discovery of India'?
items.explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru wrote 'The Discovery of India' in 1944 while imprisoned at Ahmednagar Fort. Gandhi wrote 'Hind Swaraj', Tagore wrote 'Gitanjali', and Bose is known for 'The Indian Struggle'.

items.question: Which country hosted the 2024 Summer Olympic Games?
items.explanation: The 2024 Summer Olympics were held in Paris, France. Japan hosted the previous Summer Games in Tokyo in 2021, and the United States is scheduled to host in Los Angeles in 2028.

items.question: What does CRR stand for in the context of Indian banking?
items.explanation: CRR is the Cash Reserve Ratio, the share of a bank's deposits that must be kept with the Reserve Bank of India. It is a monetary policy tool used to control liquidity, and it is distinct from the Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR).

items.question: Which body regulates the insurance sector in India?
items.explanation: The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) regulates insurers and insurance intermediaries. The RBI regulates banks, SEBI regulates securities markets, and the PFRDA regulates pension funds.

items.question: The Goods and Services Tax (GST) was launched in India in which year?
items.explanation: GST came into effect on 1 July 2017, replacing a large number of indirect taxes with a single tax. The Constitution Amendment enabling it was passed in 2016, but the tax itself launched in 2017.

items.question: Which river is known as the 'Sorrow of Bihar'?
items.explanation: The Kosi is called the Sorrow of Bihar because of its frequent and devastating floods caused by heavy silt and shifting channels. The Gandak and the Son are also Bihar rivers but do not carry this name.

items.question: Who was the first Indian woman to win an Olympic medal?
items.explanation: Karnam Malleswari won a bronze medal in weightlifting at the Sydney Olympics in 2000, becoming the first Indian woman to win an Olympic medal. P. V. Sindhu, Mary Kom and Saina Nehwal all won medals later.

items.question: The headquarters of the World Trade Organization is located in which city?
items.explanation: The World Trade Organization is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland, alongside many other international bodies. New York hosts the UN headquarters, Paris hosts UNESCO and the OECD, and Brussels hosts the European Union institutions.

items.question: Which scheme provides health insurance cover of Rs 5 lakh per family per year in India?
items.explanation: Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY) provides cashless health cover of Rs 5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary care. PM-KISAN is an income support scheme for farmers and MGNREGA is an employment guarantee scheme.

items.question: Which Indian won the Nobel Prize in Economics in 2019?
items.explanation: Abhijit Banerjee won the 2019 Nobel Prize in Economics jointly with Esther Duflo and Michael Kremer for their experimental approach to alleviating global poverty. Amartya Sen won the same prize in 1998, while Raghuram Rajan and Kaushik Basu have not won it.

items.question: The 'Bretton Woods' institutions refer to which two organisations?
items.explanation: The International Monetary Fund and the World Bank were both created at the Bretton Woods Conference in 1944. The WTO came later, in 1995, and the Asian Development Bank was founded in 1966, so neither is a Bretton Woods institution.

items.question: Which article of the Indian Constitution deals with the Right to Education?
items.explanation: Article 21A, inserted by the 86th Constitutional Amendment in 2002, makes free and compulsory education a fundamental right for children aged 6 to 14. Article 21 is the right to life and personal liberty, and Article 32 is the right to constitutional remedies.

items.question: Who is the author of the book 'Why Nations Fail'?
items.explanation: Daron Acemoglu and James Robinson wrote 'Why Nations Fail' in 2012, arguing that inclusive political and economic institutions drive prosperity. Amartya Sen wrote 'Development as Freedom', Piketty wrote 'Capital in the Twenty-First Century', and Stiglitz wrote 'Globalization and Its Discontents'.

items.question: Which country was the largest producer of crude oil in the world in 2024?
items.explanation: The United States has been the world's largest crude oil producer since 2018, driven by shale output, ahead of Saudi Arabia and Russia. Saudi Arabia leads OPEC production, but US output is higher in total.

items.question: The 'Basel III' norms relate to which sector?
items.explanation: Basel III is a set of international banking regulations on capital adequacy, stress testing and liquidity, issued by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision. Insurance has its own solvency norms, and telecom and aviation are governed by different regulators.

items.question: Which Indian city hosted the G20 Summit in 2023?
items.explanation: India hosted the G20 Leaders' Summit in New Delhi in September 2023, under its presidency of the group. The summit adopted the New Delhi Leaders' Declaration and admitted the African Union as a permanent member.

items.question: Who won the 2024 ICC Men's T20 World Cup?
items.explanation: India won the 2024 ICC Men's T20 World Cup by beating South Africa in the final in Barbados. It was India's second T20 World Cup title, after the inaugural edition in 2007.

items.question: The 'One Rank One Pension' scheme relates to which group?
items.explanation: One Rank One Pension ensures that armed forces personnel retiring in the same rank with the same length of service receive the same pension, regardless of retirement date. It applies to defence veterans, not to civilian government, railway or bank employees.

items.question: Which is the only Indian state that shares a border with China, Nepal and Bhutan?
items.explanation: Sikkim borders China to the north, Nepal to the west and Bhutan to the east, making it the only Indian state touching all three countries. Arunachal Pradesh borders China and Bhutan but not Nepal, Uttarakhand borders China and Nepal but not Bhutan, and Himachal Pradesh borders only China among the three.

items.question: What is the full form of NITI Aayog?
options: National Institute for Technology and Innovation
items.explanation: NITI Aayog stands for National Institution for Transforming India. It replaced the Planning Commission in 2015 as the government's policy think tank. The other expansions mix up real words but are not the official name.
